[How bacteria grow, cooperate and cheat, and how those interactions change the way
populations respond to antibiotics.]{.tagline}

I am a microbial ecologist and postdoctoral researcher in Gabriele Micali's Microbial
Ecology Lab at [IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital](https://www.humanitas.net/) in
Milan. I work with small synthetic bacterial communities, asking how cross-feeding,
public goods and cheating shape their composition, and what those interactions do to
antibiotic tolerance.

I run growth experiments in plate readers, microfluidic chambers and
continuous-culture bioreactors, and I write the analysis pipelines that turn those
time series into growth rates, lineages and dose–response curves. The code is on the
[Software](software.qmd) page.

I did my doctoral research in microbial ecology at Friedrich Schiller University
Jena and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv), where I
tested ecological theory with synthetic bacterial communities and models of
public-goods cheating. Before that I trained in ecology and evolution at Imperial
College London and in biology at the University of Hull.

## Interests

- Microbial interactions: cross-feeding, public goods, cooperation and cheating
- Bacterial growth dynamics and antibiotic tolerance
- Quantitative methods for growth-curve, timelapse and bioreactor data
- Open, reproducible analysis tooling in R and Python
